items.subtitle: A short worked example of the study-guide layout

sections.heading: How to use this guide
sections.summary: Read this before you attempt the practice paper.
sections.body_html: This is sample content. It shows how a study guide is laid out in sections, each with a heading and some text. Replace it with your own material.

sections.heading: Section 1 — The idea
sections.body_html: A budget adds up what each part of a programme costs, then divides the total by the number of people it serves.

sections.heading: Section 2 — The method
sections.body_html:
1. List every cost line.
  2. Add them up.
  3. Divide by the number of learners.

sections.heading: Section 3 — Quick reference
sections.body_html:
StepWhat you do
1List the costs
2Total them
3Divide per learner

items.title: Sample practice paper — Topic 1: planning a training budget
items.instructions: Sample paper. Attempt it under timed conditions (90 minutes). All amounts are in rand.
items.scenario_html: A sample organisation plans a training programme for 20 learners. The facilitator costs R40 000, the venue R15 000, materials R8 000, catering R12 000 and assessment R5 000. A contingency of 10% is added to the total.

solution_notes.recap: Five cost lines, a 10% contingency and 20 learners.
solution_notes.triggers: Total the lines before the contingency is added.
solution_notes.traps: Adding the contingency to one line instead of the total.
solution_notes.answers: Total budget R88 000; cost per learner R4 400.

parts.required: Calculate the total budget, including the contingency.
Calculate the cost per learner, before and after the contingency.
Explain why a contingency is added to a budget.

rubric.point: Costs can turn out higher than planned.
A contingency keeps the programme running when they do.
It is a percentage of the total, not of one line.

parts.required: Name two ways to reduce the cost per learner.

rubric.point: Train more learners with the same fixed costs.
Reduce or share one of the cost lines.

parts.required: Explain which costs are fixed and which change with the number of learners.

rubric.point: The facilitator and venue are fixed for the programme.
Materials and catering change with the number of learners.
